newsitem.title: ITALY: Prodi, Berlusconi talks end, no comment.
newsitem.headline: Prodi, Berlusconi talks end, no comment.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi and opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi ended talks lasting about 90 minutes on Friday, with Berlusconi declining comment to reporters as he left the meeting.
The talks at Prodi's office came a day after Berlusconi, a former prime minister, offered the government a deal on welfare reforms to boost Italy's EMU hopes.

In a letter to the newspaper L'Unita on Thursday, Berlusconi proposed striking "a transparent compromise" with the government and establishing an "understanding for Europe" to help meet the EMU commitments while reforming Italy's welfare state.
Prodi's centre-left government said on Wednesday announced it was drawing up a mini-budget to ensure it would be ready for European economic and monetary union in 1999.
